signal_confirmations.visual_evidence: Many buttons, navigation items, and interactive labels (e.g., 'Get Directions', 'Chai', '260+ Happy Customers') have a distinct pill-shaped form with near-circular border-radius.
The dominant accent colors are earthy browns, whites, oranges, and reds; no prominent purple or violet tones are visible.
The hero background is a blurred photographic image of food, without any mesh gradient or aurora blob effects.
Cards in the hero section, the 'Today's Offer' and 'Crowd Signal' boxes, and the 'STEP' cards all prominently feature a frosted glass or backdrop blur effect.
While many headings are centered, 'Dynamic Entry' and 'Current Branch And The Next Stops' are clearly left-aligned.
Sections with multiple cards use standard grid layouts or linear arrangements, lacking the varied sizing and overlapping characteristics of a bento grid.
The main headline, 'Taste the Pause Between Destinations.', is rendered in a solid light color without any gradient effect.
Small labels like 'Dynamic Entry' and 'OPEN NOW' are positioned as floating badges above and within the hero section's main heading card.
The hero background appears to be a static image with CSS-based blurring, showing no visual indicators of canvas or WebGL rendering.
All visible interactive UI elements (buttons, cards, inputs) appear to be standard HTML components, not rendered within a canvas layer.
While effects like blur and subtle gradients are present, visual inspection alone cannot confirm if they are applied via dynamically injected inline styles rather than CSS classes or static styles.
